title: The 10 Best Cordless Circular Saws
subtitle: Battery-powered saws ranked from live Amazon data — cut anywhere, no cord.
intro: A cordless circular saw trades a little sustained power for the freedom to cut anywhere — up a ladder, out in the yard, on a job site with no outlet. The catch is the battery: most of the best cordless saws sell as a bare tool (no battery or charger), which is a bargain if you already own that brand's packs and a trap if you don't. Each pick below says whether it's a bare tool or a ready-to-use kit, and which battery platform it rides. Want the most power for the least money? See the corded list.

products.name: DEWALT DCS391B 20V MAX 6-1/2" Circular Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The best-selling cordless saw here by a mile — 11,000+ reviews at 4.6 stars. Fast, well-balanced, and it rides the huge DEWALT 20V MAX platform. It's a bare tool, so you'll need a battery.
pros: 11,141 reviews at 4.6 stars — the proven pick
Runs on the massive DEWALT 20V MAX lineup
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
6-1/2" blade cuts shallower than a 7-1/4"

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ P505 18V 5-1/2" Circular Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The cheapest way into a cordless saw — if you're on RYOBI ONE+. The 5-1/2" blade is light and handy for plywood, trim, and breaking down sheet goods. A bare tool, so grab a ONE+ battery.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
5-1/2" blade limits cut depth

products.name: DEWALT DCS570B 20V MAX XR Brushless 7-1/4" Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The best cordless saw money can buy short of a FLEXVOLT. A brushless motor spins a full 7-1/4" blade at 5,500 rpm with an electric brake and a 57° bevel — near-corded performance with no cord.
pros: Full 7-1/4" blade and 5,500 rpm from a battery
Brushless motor plus an electric brake
cons: Priciest here, and it's a bare tool
Chews through batteries faster than a 6-1/2"

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX 5-1/2" Circular Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: A light, simple cordless saw on the popular BLACK+DECKER 20V platform. Great for plywood and DIY cuts around the house, with 4,000+ reviews behind it — just add a battery.
pros: 4,200 reviews on a common home battery platform
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
5-1/2" blade, light-duty only

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 RP 7-1/4" Brushless Circular Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: A full 7-1/4" brushless cordless saw for under $100 as a bare tool. On the CRAFTSMAN V20 platform, it's a lot of blade for the money if you've got the batteries.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
Smaller review base than the DEWALT

products.name: Milwaukee M18 2630-20 6-1/2" Circular Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The pick for anyone already on Milwaukee M18. Solid and well-balanced for a bare tool; not the fastest, but it taps into one of the best battery platforms out there.
pros: Runs on the excellent Milwaukee M18 system
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
3,500 rpm is on the slower side

products.name: WORX 20V 6-1/2" Cordless Circular Saw (WX526L)
products.verdict: A capable 6-1/2" cordless saw on the WORX Power Share 20V platform, spinning up to 4,700 rpm. A newer listing, but a full-size blade at a fair bare-tool price.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
Small review base so far

products.name: DEKOPRO 20V 6-1/2" Cordless Circular Saw Kit
products.verdict: The cheapest full-size cordless saw that actually comes with a battery. A 6-1/2" blade, charger, and pack in the box for around $90 — genuinely ready to cut out of the box, no platform required.
pros: Battery and charger included — no platform needed
cons: Off-brand batteries with no wider ecosystem
Generic support

products.name: WORKPRO 20V 4-1/2" Cordless Mini Circular Saw Kit
products.verdict: A one-handed mini saw that ships with a big 4.0Ah battery. Great for plywood, laminate, and paneling in tight spots — just not deep enough for framing lumber.
pros: Includes a large 4.0Ah battery and charger
Light one-handed body with a laser guide
cons: 4-1/2" blade can't cut a 2x4 in one pass
Not a full-size saw replacement

products.name: GALAX PRO 20V 4-1/2" Cordless Mini Circular Saw Kit
products.verdict: A cheap mini saw that comes with a battery and two blades. Handy one-handed for plywood, PVC, and flooring — know the limit: a 4-1/2" blade won't cut through a 2x4 in one pass.
pros: Battery, charger, and two blades included
Light one-handed body with a laser guide
cons: 4-1/2" blade, light-duty only
Lowest rating here at 4.2 stars

avoid.name: Bigheimer 4" "Mini Circular Saw" / Cut-Off Tool
avoid.flag: A 4" angle grinder with a saw guard — cuts 5/8" deep
avoid.verdict: This isn't a circular saw — it's a 4-inch angle grinder with a saw guard bolted on. It cuts 5/8 of an inch deep and spins at grinder speed. Wrong, and genuinely unsafe, for the work a circular saw does.
reasons: It cuts only 5/8 inch (16 mm) deep. A real circular saw cuts about 2-1/2 inches — enough to crosscut a 2x4 in one pass. At 5/8", it can't cut through standard lumber at all.
It's a 4-inch angle grinder with a saw guard, spinning at 12,000 RPM. Real circular saws run around 5,000-5,800 RPM; a wood blade at grinder speed is a kickback and injury risk.
No-name "Bigheimer" brand, sold tool-only (needs a DEWALT battery), and the lowest star rating in the category at 3.5.
If you want to cut metal or tile, buy a grinder. To cut wood, buy a real circular saw.

buyers_guide.a: This is the biggest trap in cordless saw listings. A 'bare tool' or 'tool only' saw ships with no battery or charger — a bargain if you already own that brand's packs, useless out of the box if you don't. A 'kit' includes a battery and charger. Every pick above says which it is.

A cordless saw is only as good as its batteries. Buying one on the same platform as a drill or driver you already own (DEWALT 20V MAX, Milwaukee M18, RYOBI ONE+, CRAFTSMAN V20) means one battery lineup for everything — a real reason to stay in one brand.

buyers_guide.q: Will cordless keep up with corded?
buyers_guide.a: For most cuts, yes — especially brushless 7-1/4" saws like the DEWALT DCS570. But a corded 15-amp saw still gives more sustained power for the money on long rips and thick stock. If you don't need portability, corded is cheaper and stronger.

6-1/2 inch is the common cordless size — light, with enough depth for 2x lumber in one pass. 7-1/4 inch cordless saws match corded cut depth but drain batteries faster. 4-1/2 inch minis are for plywood, trim, and flooring, not framing.

Plenty of cheap 'mini' cordless saws in the search results have 4-1/2" or smaller blades and can't cut through a 2x4. They're fine for sheet goods and flooring, but don't buy one expecting a full-size saw — and steer clear of grinders dressed up as saws.
